# Strings the environment-name rule finds in the driver that are not environment variables: error
# and constant names of the libraries the driver bundles, log tags, option names. Exact strings
# only, each with its reason, so a new string under a scanned prefix always fails verification until
# a reviewer classifies it, and a string the driver no longer holds fails until its row is removed.
# A variable never goes here: it goes in refused-environment.txt or known-environment.txt. Reviewed
# on every driver update.
#
# A string only some platforms' drivers hold carries "# only in <platform>,...", optionally
# followed by "; <reason>": it need not be found on the platforms the list leaves out, and must not
# be, so the row classifies it only where it was reviewed (each macOS slice is its own platform,
# osx_amd64 for x86_64 and osx_arm64 for arm64). The platforms are the lock's.
#
# A tail is the end of a longer string in the driver (the linker may store one literal as the
# tail of another, so the scan reads every tail), and is not a name of its own.
#
# string  reason

AWS_AUTH_CANONICAL_REQUEST_MISMATCH  AWS SDK error name
